ITEM.PTXT: A compact, lightweight plastic hot-wire type plug-in air flow meter has been adopted.

The hot-wire type plug-in air flow meter passes part of the intake air through the detection section and directly measures the mass flow rate, improving detection accuracy and reducing intake resistance.

It uses bypass flow measurement, which is less affected by intake pulsation from the air cleaner. Also, low loss is achieved by a flow passage structure with low fluid resistance, allowing air volumes from small to large to be measured reliably.

MECA.TITLE: Hot-wire Type Air Flow Meter Operation

ITEM.PTXT: Part of the intake air is bypassed and the intake air volume is measured at the hot wire measuring section. The hot wire measuring section uses a platinum filament (platinum hot wire), and a bridge circuit is formed by the hot wires of the intake air temperature measuring resistor and the heating resistor (heater) to measure the engine intake air volume. Due to the characteristics of the hot-wire type air flow meter, the mass flow rate can in principle be measured directly, so density correction for changes in intake air temperature is not necessary; however, intake air temperature information is required for engine controls such as EFI. Therefore, a compact thermistor type intake air temperature sensor is built into the air flow meter to detect the intake air temperature.
A bridge circuit is a circuit connected as shown in the illustration below, in which, when R1 × R4 = R2 × R3 holds, V1 = V2 and the value indicated by ammeter G is 0.

When the intake air volume changes, the bridge circuit of the hot wire measuring section feedback-controls the power supplied to the heating resistor so that the temperature difference between the intake air temperature measuring resistor and the heating resistor (heater) is always kept constant. This supplied power is converted into a voltage and output to the engine control computer. The engine control computer calculates the engine intake air volume from the predetermined relationship between the air flow meter output voltage and flow rate.

A highly accurate electromagnetic pickup type sensor has been adopted. Performs cylinder identification and detection of actual camshaft timing.

The camshaft position sensor is installed at the rear end of the cylinder head and detects the protrusions of the camshaft timing rotor (360-180-180°CA) fixed to the intake camshaft. As the camshaft rotates, the air gap between the timing rotor protrusions and the camshaft position sensor changes, so the magnetic flux passing through the coil of the camshaft position sensor increases and decreases, generating an electromotive force in the coil. This generated voltage is reversed when the timing rotor protrusion approaches and when it moves away from the camshaft position sensor, so it appears as an AC voltage.
A highly accurate electromagnetic pickup type sensor has been adopted. Detects the crank position and crank angular velocity.
The crankshaft timing rotor installed on the crankshaft has 34 signal teeth with 2 teeth missing for top dead center detection.

The crankshaft position sensor detects the crank rotation signal every 10° and can accurately detect top dead center from the location of the missing teeth. A sensor similar to the camshaft position sensor has been adopted, detecting the signal as AC power.

A non-contact type accelerator position sensor has been adopted, using a Hall element that can extract the magnetic field strength as an electrical signal using the Hall effect, which provides an output voltage linear to the accelerator pedal depression amount. When the accelerator pedal depression amount changes, the angle of the magnetic field relative to the flow of the applied current in the Hall element changes, so the strength of the magnetic field perpendicular to the applied current changes. The resulting change in voltage, generated perpendicular to both the applied current and the magnetic field, is sent to the engine control computer as the accelerator pedal depression amount signal. In addition, reliability is ensured by adopting a 2-system (main and sub) sensor with different output characteristics.

ITEM.PTXT: A non-contact type throttle position sensor has been adopted, using a Hall element that can extract the magnetic field strength as an electrical signal using the Hall effect, which provides an output voltage linear to the throttle valve opening angle. When the throttle valve opening angle changes, the angle of the magnetic field relative to the flow of the applied current in the Hall element changes, so the strength of the magnetic field perpendicular to the applied current changes. As a result, the change in voltage generated perpendicular to both the applied current and the magnetic field is sent to the engine control computer as the throttle valve opening angle signal. In addition, reliability is ensured by adopting a 2-system (main and sub) sensor with different output characteristics.

ENTRY.PTXT: If a malfunction occurs in either or both circuits, the engine control computer detects the malfunction from the voltage difference between the main circuit and sub circuit. At this time, power to the throttle motor is cut and the throttle valve is returned to a predetermined opening angle by the return spring. Limp mode driving is made possible by controlling engine output using fuel injection control and ignition timing control. ITEM.PTXT: A 1-valve type electronically controlled throttle body, in which the throttle valve is driven by a motor, has been adopted.
A flat shaft has been adopted to increase the opening area of the valve, improving performance.

The driver's operation (accelerator pedal depression amount) is transmitted to the engine control computer by the accelerator position sensor located on the accelerator pedal. The engine control computer determines the throttle opening appropriate to the driving conditions and drives the throttle motor. The throttle valve opening is fed back to the engine control computer by the throttle position sensor.

The throttle valve drive motor is mounted on the throttle body, and the opening and closing of the throttle valve is controlled through reduction gears. In addition, a DC motor with good response and low power consumption has been adopted.
The inside of the throttle position sensor has a 2-system (main and sub) configuration, and the system is constantly monitored for malfunctions.

If a malfunction is detected, the warning light in the meter alerts the driver and current to the motor is cut. At this time, the throttle valve is returned to a predetermined opening by the throttle valve return spring, and engine output is adjusted according to the accelerator opening through fuel injection cut and ignition retard, enabling limp-home driving.
Detects the engine coolant temperature and sends a signal to the engine control computer.
Converts the oxygen concentration in the exhaust gas into an electromotive force and detects whether the air-fuel ratio is rich or lean relative to the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio.
By heating the sensor (zirconia element) with a built-in heater, the O2sensor temperature is kept constant, promoting feedback control.

An A/F sensor has been adopted to reliably feed back the air-fuel ratio condition from the exhaust gas. A laminated sensor structure has been adopted to promote early activation of the sensor, achieving air-fuel ratio feedback control from immediately after engine start.

Unlike a sensor that outputs a lean or rich signal at the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio boundary, i.e. the O2sensor, the A/F sensor has output characteristics proportional to the air-fuel ratio, enabling the engine control computer to perform more precise air-fuel ratio control.

To activate the A/F sensor, the sensor (zirconia element) must be heated. While a cup type sensor requires time to activate because it is heated indirectly through an atmospheric layer, a laminated type sensor heats the zirconia element directly, shortening the sensor activation time. In addition, the heat mass has been reduced by downsizing the zirconia element.
A flat (non-resonant type) knock sensor has been adopted.

When the knock sensor receives vibration from the cylinder block, the movement of the weight lags due to inertia. As a result, pressure is applied to the piezoelectric ceramic provided between the cylinder block and the weight, generating voltage. The voltage is output almost constantly across all frequency bands, and the engine control computer detects the target frequency and determines that knocking is occurring.
The position of the spool valve is controlled by the duty signal from the ECU to regulate the oil supply to the advance and retard chambers of the VVT-i controller.

A 12-hole ultra-fine atomization injector has been adopted. It is mounted directly to the cylinder head, shortening the distance to the combustion chamber and reducing fuel adhesion to the intake port, for excellent fuel economy and emission performance.
A circumferential flow type in-tank fuel pump has been adopted.
By integrating the charcoal canister, fuel filter and pressure regulator into the fuel pump assembly, the number of parts and weight have been reduced and space in the engine room has been saved.
By placing a coil independently for each cylinder, the distributor and high-tension cords are eliminated, reducing losses in the high-voltage section, ensuring reliability and reducing radio noise.
A compact, lightweight igniter is built in, and a high voltage is induced in the secondary (No. 2) coil by the signal from the engine control computer.
The canister purge volume is controlled by the signal (duty signal) from the engine control computer. The purge volume is determined by the ratio of the ON and OFF times of the signal (duty ratio).
The piping of the canister purge VSV has been optimized to reduce evaporative pulsation noise.
The EFI-L method, which detects the intake air volume with the air flow meter and controls the fuel injection volume, has been adopted.
Independent injection (each cylinder injected 1 time(s) per 2 crankshaft revolutions) has been adopted as the injection method.

Fuel injection consists of synchronous injection, in which the basic injection duration is corrected with signals from each sensor and fuel is always injected at the same position, and asynchronous injection, in which fuel is injected when an injection request is detected from the signals of each sensor regardless of crank angle. Also, to protect the engine and improve fuel economy, fuel cut is performed to temporarily stop fuel injection according to driving conditions.

The engine speed is measured for a certain period, and if there is a difference from the target speed, the throttle valve opening is controlled to bring the idle speed to the target value.

ITEM.PTXT: VVT-i, which continuously varies the camshaft phase, has been adopted, and by adjusting the intake valve timing according to the driving conditions, both low fuel consumption and high output as well as low emissions are achieved.
The spool valve of the OCV moves to the left, hydraulic pressure is applied to the advance chamber of the VVT-i controller, and the intake camshaft rotates in the advance direction.
The spool valve of the OCV moves to the right, hydraulic pressure is applied to the retard chamber of the VVT-i controller, and the intake camshaft rotates in the retard direction.
The hydraulic pressure in the advance and retard chambers of the VVT-i controller is held as it is, and the phase of the intake camshaft is also held.
By continuously varying the camshaft phase and adjusting the valve timing according to the driving conditions, both low fuel consumption and high output as well as low emissions are achieved.

MECA.TITLE: Valve, Valve Lifter and Valve Spring

ITEM.PTXT: The intake valves and exhaust valves have been nitrided over their entire surface to ensure wear resistance. Also, weight has been reduced by making the stems smaller in diameter.
The exhaust valves have been heat treated (solution aging treatment) to cope with the rise in exhaust temperature due to higher performance.

Shimless type valve lifters with a large effective area have been adopted to accommodate high lift. Also, the top surface has been treated with Fericoat (molybdenum-containing iron phosphate coating) to ensure reliability and reduce friction.
The valve springs use high-strength material and are nitrided for higher strength, and have a thin wire diameter and uneven pitch to improve valve follow-up, achieve high lift and reduce weight.

ITEM.PTXT: A vane-type VVT-i controller has been provided on the intake camshaft.
It consists of a housing fixed to the timing gear and a vane fixed to the camshaft.

By applying oil pressure from the OCV (oil control valve) to the advance chamber and retard chamber of the VVT-i controller, the vane is rotated, continuously varying the phase of the intake camshaft.
When the engine is stopped, it is locked at the most retarded position by the lock pin. When the engine starts, the lock pin is released by oil pressure.

ITEM.PTXT: The position of the spool valve is controlled by the duty signal from the ECU to regulate the oil supply to the advance and retard chambers of the VVT-i controller.
The speed of the 2 cooling fan motors is switched in 2 stages according to the coolant temperature and air conditioner operating status.
The 2 motors are connected in series (6V) at Lo and in parallel (12V) at Hi.
A system in which the engine control computer directly controls relay ON/OFF has been adopted.
Turns the fuel pump ON and OFF based on the starter signal and engine speed signal.

In addition to when the engine is stopped, when the airbag deployment signal from the airbag ECU is input to the engine control computer upon airbag deployment, the fuel pump is stopped to minimize fuel leakage.
A circumferential flow type in-tank fuel pump has been adopted.
By integrating the charcoal canister, fuel filter and pressure regulator into the fuel pump assembly, the number of parts and weight have been reduced and space in the engine room has been saved.

By passing current through the heater to warm the zirconia element, stable oxygen concentration feedback is performed even when the exhaust gas temperature is low, such as immediately after engine start, reducing emissions.

Canister purge control, which draws fuel vapor generated in the fuel tank into the intake port for combustion, has been adopted. The canister purge volume is flow-controlled by the engine control computer, which controls the opening and closing of the canister purge VSV according to the driving conditions.
Canister purge control, which draws fuel evaporative gas generated from the fuel tank into the intake port and burns it, has been adopted.
Integrated with the fuel pump and located inside the fuel tank. This reduces the number of parts, making the fuel system lighter and more compact.
The canister purge volume is controlled by the signal (duty signal) from the engine control computer. The purge volume is determined by the ratio of the ON and OFF times of the signal (duty ratio).
The piping of the canister purge VSV has been optimized to reduce evaporative pulsation noise.
Cranking hold control has been adopted on all models.

When the start signal (STSW) from the start switch is input, the engine control computer sends a signal (STAR) to the starter relay through the neutral start switch (determining P or N position) to operate the starter. At this time, the engine control computer turns ON the ACC cut (ACCR) to prevent flickering of the meter, clock, audio, etc.

After the starter starts operating, the engine control computer continues to output a signal to the starter until it detects that the engine has started running. When it determines that the engine has started running, the engine control computer stops outputting the signal to the starter relay.
A compact, lightweight, high-output, high-efficiency PS (Planetary reduction-Segment conductor motor) starter has been adopted.
A rectangular conductor armature coil has been adopted to reduce size and weight.
By using bare rectangular wire for the armature coil, the space factor has been improved, increasing starter torque.
The cylindrical commutator has been eliminated, shortening the armature shaft length.
Interpolar magnets have been adopted between the field coils. This improves the magnetic circuit and increases the magnetic flux, allowing size reduction and shortening the yoke axial length.

By lowering the generated voltage during vehicle acceleration and raising it during deceleration, the engine load caused by alternator power generation is reduced, improving fuel economy. In addition, during idling and constant-speed driving, the generated voltage is adjusted so that the integrated current value approaches the target value.
The integrated current value is the integrated value of the battery input/output current detected by the current sensor.

Installed on the negative terminal of the battery, it detects the battery charge/discharge current and sends a signal to the engine control computer. Based on this signal, the engine control computer calculates the battery capacity. A Hall IC is used to detect the charge/discharge current; it converts the change in magnetic flux density generated in the core by the battery charge/discharge current into a voltage and outputs it.

If the battery fluid temperature is too low or too high, it can accelerate battery deterioration or cause the battery to discharge. Also, since the current acceptance characteristics change with battery fluid temperature, the battery is protected by detecting the battery fluid temperature and sending a signal to the engine control computer.
The battery temperature sensor is built into the battery current sensor and is located near the negative terminal, where it is less affected by engine heat.

When a sensor malfunctions, or when the engine control computer judges it necessary based on battery condition, electrical load operating status, etc., alternator charging control is stopped and the system switches to constant voltage generation mode.

ENTRY.PTXT: The state of charge is judged from the battery capacity and fluid temperature, and charging control is stopped during overcharge or overdischarge to protect the battery and prevent capacity reduction.
When Battery Fluid Temperature Is Low or High
When Wipers Are Operating or Blower Motor Is Operating Under High Load

When the power supply voltage changes due to the operation of electrical equipment, the alternator generated voltage changes due to charging control. To prevent an unnatural feeling while driving due to the resulting change in engine load, charging control is temporarily stopped.

When a malfunction is detected in any of the following sensors and switches: current sensor, temperature sensor, vehicle speed sensor, throttle position sensor, crank angle sensor, stop light switch, neutral start switch
When a sensor system malfunctions, charging control is stopped to prevent a decrease in battery capacity.
Prevents a decrease in battery capacity due to the vehicle being left unused, protecting the battery.
When 2 Hours Have Elapsed During Charging Control
The charge capacity is checked periodically and errors in the integrated current value caused by long periods of charging and discharging are corrected, preventing a decrease in battery capacity.
When Cumulative Operating Time Reaches 20 Hours
Sufficient charging is performed periodically to prevent a reduction in battery life caused by repeated charging and discharging.
